title: Parsnip and puy lentil pot with cavolo nero

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or a plain cupboard staple, and vegetable stock and wholegrain mustard are both allowed.

supermarket.reason: Puy lentils, cavolo nero, parsnips and crème fraîche are all everyday lines at Tesco and similar shops.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a lidded saucepan, a knife and a grater, with simple frying and simmering.

works.reason: 200g puy lentils and 500g parsnips in 900ml stock, simmered for 25 minutes and finished with mustard, crème fraîche and lemon, gives a well-seasoned, brothy pot for four.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes covers slicing the leeks and peeling and chopping the parsnips while the leeks soften, and 35 minutes cook matches the boil, 25-minute simmer and 5 minutes for the greens.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears beyond a splash of water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm lentil pot suits early October, and the 500g of parsnips are the bulk of the dish rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, plainly worded British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Lentils, root veg and greens make a filling, wholesome lunch a family would happily eat again.
